title: WHEN THE CURSE KEEPS COMING OUT AS BLESSING

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The people rise like a lioness; they rouse themselves like a lion that does not rest till it devours its prey and drinks the blood of its victims." Then Balak said to Balaam, "Neither curse them at all nor bless them at all!" Balaam answered, "Did I not tell you I must do whatever the LORD says?" - Num 23:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The second oracle ends with an image of strength: Israel rising like a lion, unstoppable in God's purpose. This was the very opposite of what Balak wanted to hear. Twice now the curse has come out as blessing, and the king has had enough. In frustration he cries out, if Balaam cannot curse them, then let him say nothing at all!

Balak would rather have silence than blessing. But Balaam reminds him of what he has said from the start: he must do whatever the Lord says. The prophet is not free to bless or curse or stay silent at will. He is bound to the word of God, whatever Balak prefers.

There is a quiet lesson here about the futility of fighting God. Balak keeps striving against a purpose he cannot change, growing more frustrated with each attempt. All his effort accomplishes nothing except to display, again and again, the unstoppable blessing of God upon His people.

How much better to align ourselves with God's purposes than to exhaust ourselves opposing them. In Christ, we discover that God's will is not our enemy but our greatest good. Rather than striving against Him like Balak, we are invited to rest in the blessing He delights to give (Rom 8:31). Stop fighting God, and receive what He longs to pour out.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you exhausting yourself fighting against God's purposes?
2. How does aligning with God's will bring rest rather than frustration?
3. What blessing might God be longing to give that you have resisted?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from wearing myself out in opposition to Your will. Help me to align my heart with Your purposes and to rest in the blessing You delight to give in Christ. Amen.
